title: Manning's Equation (Open Channel)

S.description: Bed slope (energy gradient for uniform flow)

applicability: Primary design equation for canals. Uniform flow assumed. For trapezoidal section: A = (b + z×y) × y, P = b + 2y√(1+z²), where b = bottom width, y = depth, z = side slope (H:V).

title: Tractive Force — Boundary Shear Stress

τ₀.description: Average boundary shear stress on bed

applicability: For stable channel design: τ₀ ≤ τ_cr (critical tractive stress of boundary material). Bank shear ≈ 0.75 × τ₀ for trapezoidal channels. Side slope stability also requires τ_bank ≤ τ_cr × K where K = tractive force ratio = √(1 - sin²φ_s/sin²φ), φ_s = side slope angle, φ = repose angle.

title: Lacey Regime — Wetted Perimeter
applicability: For alluvial canals carrying sediment-laden water. Developed from Indian subcontinent canal data. Used with other Lacey equations (R, S, V) to establish regime dimensions.

title: Lacey Regime — Hydraulic Radius and Slope

f.description: Lacey silt factor: f = 1.76 × √(d_m), d_m = median particle size in mm

applicability: f values: 0.4 (very fine silt), 0.7 (fine silt), 1.0 (medium sand ~0.32 mm), 1.5 (coarse sand), 2.0 (gravel). Only valid for alluvial channels in regime.

title: Kennedy's Critical Velocity

m.description: Critical velocity ratio (CVR): 1.0 for standard silt, 0.7–0.9 for fine, 1.1–1.3 for coarse

applicability: Empirical — developed for Upper Bari Doab Canal system (Punjab). Used in conjunction with Manning's equation to solve for b and y. Does not give channel shape — must assume b/y ratio.

title: Best Hydraulic Section — Trapezoidal

b.description: Bottom width for best hydraulic section

R.description: Hydraulic radius = y/2 for all best sections

applicability: Optimal z = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577 (60° from horizontal) gives half-hexagon. In practice, z is constrained by soil stability. Given a fixed z, the best b/y ratio minimizes wetted perimeter for a given area.

title: Seepage Loss — Moritz Empirical Formula

q_s.description: Seepage loss per unit length of canal

applicability: Quick estimate. Actual seepage depends on groundwater depth, soil permeability, canal geometry, and wetted perimeter. More rigorous analysis uses Darcy's law with seepage path geometry.

title: Superelevation in Canal Curves

Δy.description: Superelevation — difference in water surface between outer and inner banks

r_c.description: Radius of curvature of canal centerline

applicability: Add Δy to freeboard on the outer bank. Minimum radius of curvature: USBR recommends r_c ≥ 3 × T for lined canals, r_c ≥ 5 × T for unlined.
source: USBR Design of Small Canal Structures

title: Transition Energy Loss

C_t.description: Transition loss coefficient: 0.10 contraction (converging), 0.30 expansion (diverging) — USBR values

applicability: For gradual (well-designed) transitions. Abrupt transitions: C_t = 0.3 (contraction), 0.5–1.0 (expansion). Transition length: L = (T₁-T₂)/(2×tanα), where α = wall deflection angle (typically 12.5°–25°).

title: Canal Capacity with Conveyance Losses

f_loss.description: Fractional loss rate per km (seepage + evaporation)

applicability: Typical losses: unlined 2–8% per km in pervious soils; lined 0.5–2% per km. Evaporation loss usually small (0.1–0.3% per km) compared to seepage.
